web_evidence.title: The Bat Segundo Show: Patricia Cornwell
web_evidence.note: This contemporaneous interview identifies Scarpetta as Cornwell's current book and explicitly describes her mid-series switch from first to third person and inability at that time to write the series in first person.

web_evidence.title: Patricia Cornwell talks Kay Scarpetta and a life of crime novels
web_evidence.note: The Washington Post's author interview describes the series' middle phase as third person, used to inhabit other characters, followed by a later return to first person; the 2008 novel falls within that third-person phase.

person_note: The controlling narration is third person. The authorized opening excerpt narrates Scarpetta externally, while the supplied interior passages independently do the same for Marino, Lucy, and Scarpetta, including access to their sensations, thoughts, and beliefs. First-person forms in the sample occur only in dialogue or universal gnomic language, not in base narration. Author-interview evidence places the 2008 book within Cornwell's mid-series third-person phase before her later return to first person. The web excerpt covers only the opening and the structural sources discuss the series phase rather than cataloguing every chapter, but the separate Lucy passage and Chapter 32 passage provide strong interior corroboration and reveal no sustained contrary person.
